(p-400) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Al-Mursalat (The Emissaries).

His saying, exalted is He: "By those sent forth in successive waves, and those that rage in fierce gusts, and those that spread far and wide, and those that separate decisively, and those that convey a reminder, as an excuse or as a warning."

Allah swears by these named things. There is disagreement concerning "those sent forth" (al-mursalat), "those that rage" (al-'asifat), and "those that spread" (al-nashirat).

It has been said that they are the winds. It has also been said that they are the angels or the messengers. As for "'urfan," it means "in succession," like the mane of a horse (ʿurf al-faras), one after another. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah chose that they are the winds. Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas chose that they are the angels.

It is also reported from Abu Salih that they are the messengers; this was stated by Ibn Kathir, who favoured the first view and said: "Ibn Jarir held back (from deciding)." The reality is that Ibn Jarir's words indicate that he saw no barrier to intending all of them together, since the meaning is open to these possibilities and he saw no obstacle.

Ibn Kathir considered it most likely that they are the winds, based on His saying: "And We sent the winds fertilising" (Al-Hijr: 22), and His saying: "And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy" (Al-A'raf: 57).

This is what the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) chose in his book Mudhakkirat al-Imla'. As for "those that separate" (al-fariqat), it has been said that they are the angels, and it has been said that they are the verses of the Qur'an; the Shaykh preferred the first view. As for "those that convey a reminder" (al-mulqiyat dhikran), "as an excuse or as a warning":

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had already explained them in Surah As-Saffat at his saying: "By those who recite the reminder" (As-Saffat: 3).

In Mudhakkirat al-Imla', he says: "'Udhran" is a verbal noun (ism masdar) meaning "giving an excuse" (al-i'dhar), and its meaning is cutting off excuse (qat' al-'udhr). From it comes the proverb: "Whoever gives an excuse has given a warning." It is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi). "Nudhran" is also a verbal noun meaning "warning" (al-indhar), and it is likewise an object of purpose. Warning (al-indhar) is informing accompanied by threat. The "aw" (or) in His saying: (p-401) "or as a warning" is used in the sense of "wa" (and), meaning: for the sake of giving excuse and warning. The use of "aw" in the sense of "wa" is like its occurrence in the verse of 'Amr ibn Ma'd Yakrib:

"A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them between one who bridles his colt and one who restrains it,"

meaning: "and one who restrains it."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 7:

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely to occur.﴾

This is the thing sworn to (al-muqsam 'alayhi). In general there is, between every oath and what is sworn to, a connection of relevance in the overall discourse (munasaba irtibat fi al-jumla). Allah swears by whatever He wills and concerning whatever He wills, because the thing sworn by is among His creation. Thus, the choice of what is sworn by here or there generally serves some kind of relevance (munasaba). If we reflect on it here, we find that the thing sworn to is the Day of Resurrection, and they deny it. So He swears to them by that which contains the proof of His power over it: the winds, as is customary, bring the clouds and spread them, then the rain comes, and Allah gives life to the earth after its death.

This is among the proofs of the power to resurrect (al-ba'th). The violent ones among them come with great force, and they may uproot trees and demolish houses, things against which they have no strength and no power. What they contain of indication of destruction and annihilation, both of these indicate the power to resurrect.

Then the angels come with clarification, guidance, excuse and warning: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely to occur.﴾

- And Allah knows best -.

All of these are cosmic changes arising from that promised Day. The effacing of the stars (ṭamsu'l-nujūm) is the going away of their light, as in His saying: ﴿And when the stars are dispersed﴾ [At-Takwir: 2].

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ means it is rent asunder and cleft, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the sky is split apart﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1], ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1]. The blowing away of the mountains (nasf al-jibal) has had its explanation given in several places. And for them there are several stages: crushing and pulverizing, and scattering and moving, like clouds and then like mirages. This was discussed in Surah Qaf at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them?﴾ [Qaf: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 11:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already explained this in Surah "al-Waqi'ah" at His statement, may He be exalted: (p-402) ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter﴾ ﴿will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known day﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49-50].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For what day were they deferred?﴾ ﴿For the Day of Decision.﴾

The Day of Decision (yawm al-fasl) is the Day of Resurrection, on which judgment is made between the creatures, between the oppressor and the oppressed, the rightful and the falsifier, and the creditor and the debtor, as Exalted is He explained by His saying: ﴿This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and the former peoples.﴾ [al-Mursalat: 38], and like His saying: ﴿That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.﴾ [Hud: 103].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

It is a severe warning from Allah, exalted is He, to the deniers.

The meaning of this has already been discussed by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) at the end of Surah "al-Dhariyat", at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, because of their Day which they are promised.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 60]

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ ﴿Then We placed it in a firm repository,﴾ ﴿for a known period.﴾

"The despised fluid" is the mixed drop (al-nutfah al-amshaj), and "the firm repository" is the womb (al-rahim). Allah has made it firm and protected it, even from the breath of the air.

The wondrous signs in this repository are beyond description. Allah has made clear that it is the womb in His saying: ﴿And We cause to settle in the wombs what We will for an appointed term﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. "The known period" is the duration of pregnancy until a miscarriage or birth.

The Shaykh has already drawn attention to this in the beginning of Surat al-Hajj, and that these are different measures and specified terms.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We measured, and excellent are the measurers.﴾

In it is the praise of Himself for power over that, and it is the truth, and none is able to do it except Allah, as He said: ﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 58-59].

And He, exalted is He, has explained this at the beginning of surah "al-Hajj" (the Pilgrimage): ﴿Then from a clinging clot and an unformed lump﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5], to the end of the context.

(p-403) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ ﴿for the living and the dead?﴾

It has already been mentioned to the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) in Surah Ta-Ha, at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who made the earth a cradle for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53]. Al-kifat (the receptacle) is the place in which they are gathered (yaksitun, i.e., gather and hold). Al-kaft (gathering) is holding together: the living upon its back, and the dead in its bellies, as in His saying: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55]. He combined both meanings in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has produced you from the earth as a growth﴾ ﴿Then He will return you into it and bring you forth [again] in an emergence﴾ [Nuh: 17–18].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Depart toward that which you used to deny.﴾

He clarified it afterwards by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Depart toward a shadow having three branches,﴾ ﴿Neither shading nor availing against the blaze.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like forts,﴾ ﴿As if they were yellow camels.﴾ [al-Mursalat: 30-33], meaning: and it is Jahannam (Hellfire).

And He, exalted is He, has clarified in another place that they will be pushed into it with force, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing.﴾ [al-Tur: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 35:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾

He stated explicitly that they will not speak on that day, although they do speak and answer when they are questioned, as in His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24].

And His saying: ﴿So they turned to one another, blaming each other﴾ [al-Qalam: 30].

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us) had already discussed this issue in the commentary on surah al-Naml, at His saying: ﴿And the word will come into effect against them for what they did, and they will not speak﴾ [al-Naml: 85].

He explained the way of reconciling these verses by referring to the removal of the appearance of contradiction (daf' iham al-idtirab) in his commentary on surah al-Mursalat, namely that this occurs in different stations (manazil) and states (hala't).

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

Surah al-Mursalat

The words of the Exalted: ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾ ﴿Nor will they be permitted, so they could make excuses﴾.

This noble verse indicates that the people of the Fire do not speak and do not offer excuses.

Verses have come indicating that they do speak and make excuses,

• such as His saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23],

• and His saying: ﴿And they will offer peace, [saying], "We did not do any evil"﴾ [al-Nahl: 28],

• and His saying: ﴿Rather, we used not to call upon anything before﴾ [40],

• and His saying: ﴿By Allah, we were truly in manifest error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds. And none led us astray except the criminals﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97-99],

• and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us﴾ [al-A'raf: 38],

along with other verses.

The answer to this is in several respects:

The first: The Resurrection has stations (mawatin); in some of them they speak, and in some of them they do not speak.

The second: They do not speak with what would benefit them, and what has no benefit in it is as good as nonexistent.

The third: After Allah says to them: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108], their speech ceases and nothing remains but groaning (zafir) and sobbing (shahiq).

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the word will come into effect against them for what they did, and they will not speak﴾ [al-Naml: 85]. And this third aspect goes back to the first aspect.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾

In it is the explicit text that their deeds in this world are a cause of their enjoyment of the bounties of Paradise in the Hereafter. Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will be called out, "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do"﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

(p-404) And it has come in a hadith: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deed" (lan yadkhula ahadukum al-jannata bi-'amalihi). There is no contradiction between the two texts, for entry is by the bounty of Allah, and after entry there is inheritance (al-tawaruth, the inheriting of ranks), and there are degrees, and enjoyment is by means of deeds. Thus they all share in Allah's favour upon them by entering Paradise, but after entry they differ in degrees according to their deeds.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 44:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers.﴾

In the verse before it He, exalted is He, said: ﴿for what you used to do﴾ [al-Mursalat: 43]. Here He said: ﴿We reward the good-doers﴾, and He did not say "We reward the doers", which indicates that the reward is for excellence (ihsan) in action, not merely for action alone. It has already been established that the purpose of obligation (taklif) is excellence in action: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 1-2].

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had already explained this in surah "al-Kahf", at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made that which is upon the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ [al-Kahf: 7].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down.﴾

This noble verse is one of the verses used as evidence that the disbelievers are held accountable for abandoning the subsidiary rulings (furu', the detailed practical obligations of the Shari'ah). The point has been drawn attention to many times before. What is important here is that most of the subsidiary matters mentioned in the Qur'an are concerned with the prayer (salah), which confirms that it is truly the pillar (imad) of the religion.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 77, verse 50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾

That is: after this noble Qur'an, because of the signs, proofs and admonitions it contains, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6].

And He, exalted is He, has made clear that He sent it down as the best statement (ahsan al-hadith) of guidance, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent within itself and repeating [its teachings]. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills﴾ [az-Zumar: 23].

Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir, mentioned from Ibn Abi Hatim, up to Abu Hurayrah, narrating: "When one recites ﴿By those sent forth in gusts﴾ and then recites ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾, let him say: 'I believe in Allah and what He has sent down.'" (p. 405) He also mentioned in the surah "al-Qiyamah," from Abu Dawud and Ahmad, several hadiths through several chains that he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites in the surah al-Insan (the surah of Man) ﴿Is not He who can give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 40], let him say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, yes indeed.' And when he recites the surah 'at-Tin' and arrives at His saying ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [at-Tin: 8], let him say: 'Yes, and I am of those who bear witness to that.' And whoever recites ﴿By those sent forth﴾ and reaches ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾, let him say: 'We believe in Allah.'" End of quotation.

We say: "We believe in Allah," as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us.
